question: The Commission’s proposal to reform the common agricultural policy (CAP) from 2028 and introduce the National and Regional Partnership Fund (NRP Fund) provides for capping and degressivity of direct payments. Under the current design of the CAP, funds freed up as a result of capping remained within the respective region and corresponding support area and could still be used there for agricultural policy purposes.

Under the new governance structure of the National and Regional Partnership Plans (NRPs), there are questions as to how the geographical and administrative distribution of funds will work in the future. 1.
Do funds freed up as a result of capping direct payments also remain within the same region under the NRP funds?

How does the Commission define the term ‘region’ in this context? Does it refer to the Member State as a whole, to regional administrative units (e.g. the Länder in Germany) or to other land divisions?
If the funds no longer necessarily remain within the same region, what are the criteria for redistribution within the respective NRP Plan in the future?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.8.2026) 1. Funds freed up as a result of degressivity and capping remains at Member State level within the budget ring-fenced for certain agricultural interventions. According to the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP) legislative proposal of July 20251, Member States have a large flexibility to re-allocate these funds.

Accordingly, a Member State can decide that funds freed up as a result of degressivity and capping remain within the same area or region. 2. Because of the large flexibility regarding the geographical distribution, as referred above, the Commission proposal does not define ‘region’ in the context of degressive area based income support. 3.

There are no criteria set at EU level for the targeting of funds freed up as a result of capping and degressivity. Member States may decide to reallocate such funds to income support interventions such as coupled income support, climate and agri-environment actions or investments, in line with their policy priorities as defined in national and regional partnership plans.
